title: Shallow M7 pairs within 300 km showed no clear excess at 30-180 days under five-year shuffles in 1976-2025
abstract: We tested whether shallow earthquakes of magnitude 7 or more occur near each other at delays longer than one month. A fixed USGS ComCat record gave 530 events in 1976-2025. There were 44 pairs within 300 km and more than 30 to 180 days apart. We kept event dates fixed and shuffled locations within five-year periods. In 19,999 draws, the mean count was 39.80 and the 95% reference range was 29-52. The upper-tail p value was 0.25775. The result did not show a clear excess under this reference. The expected count rose to 70.52 for one-year periods and fell to 34.28 for ten-year periods. In contrast, 48 pairs occurred within seven days, against a five-year shuffle mean of 2.84. This small study gives a reproducible delay test and shows its dependence on the reference time scale. It does not exclude delayed interactions, test distant triggering, or estimate a change in hazard. Source rows, hashes, all pair lists, null draws, code, a figure, and a separate arithmetic audit are supplied.

display.caption: Nearby pair counts in 530 shallow M7 events from 1976-2025. The primary delay count is inside the five-year location-shuffle reference range. Shorter delay counts are above their reference ranges. The ranges are null percentiles, not effect confidence limits.
Changing the shuffle period changes the expected delayed pair count. Null reference ranges are not effect confidence limits.
